root_cause.text: The functions `scx_group_set_weight()`, `scx_group_set_idle()`, and `scx_group_set_bandwidth()` cache the global `scx_root` pointer into a local variable before acquiring the `scx_cgroup_ops_rwsem` lock, allowing the pointer to become stale and point to a freed scheduler if a scheduler disable/enable sequence occurs before the lock is acquired.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the assignment `sch = scx_root;` was moved from before `percpu_down_read(&scx_cgroup_ops_rwsem);` to after it in all three functions, ensuring that the scheduler pointer is read only after the lock is held. The commit message confirms that this prevents a Use-After-Free (UAF) on `SCX_HAS_OP(sch, ...)` and `SCX_CALL_OP(sch, ...)`.
